title: Classic Roast Chicken
subtitle: Simple butter-basted whole chicken with lemon and herbs
excerpt: A good roast chicken needs three things: butter under the skin, a hot oven, and a proper rest. This version uses lemon, garlic, and thyme for a clean, classic result.
sourceNotes: British roast chicken method. Internal temperature check is the most reliable way to confirm doneness.

content.text: Take the chicken out of the fridge an hour before roasting. A cold bird going into a hot oven can cook unevenly.

items.prepNote: halved; one half for the cavity, one for the tin

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Rest the chicken at room temperature for 1 hour before cooking.
Mix the softened butter with the leaves from 2 thyme sprigs. Season well.
Loosen the skin over the breast by sliding your fingers underneath. Push the herb butter beneath the skin and spread it evenly.
Stuff the cavity with one lemon half, the garlic, and the remaining thyme and rosemary.
Place the chicken in the roasting tin. Season the skin generously.
Roast for 20 minutes per 500g plus 20 minutes. For a 1.5kg chicken this is about 80 minutes.
Check the thickest part of the thigh with a probe thermometer. It should read 75 degrees C.
Rest uncovered for 15 minutes before carving.

items.symptom: Breast meat is dry but legs are still pink.
items.cause: Chicken started cold or oven ran too hot.
items.fix: Always rest at room temperature first; use a probe to check legs.

items.symptom: Skin is pale and not crispy.
items.cause: Moisture on the surface or oven not hot enough.
items.fix: Pat skin very dry before buttering; increase heat for the last 10 minutes.

items.cause: Not fully cooked; thermometer is the only reliable check.
items.fix: Return to the oven for 10 more minutes and re-check temperature.
